Regularized incomplete gamma function (C backend)

Source: R/core_stats.R
cgamcdf.Rd

The lower regularized incomplete gamma function \(P(a, x)\), which is the CDF of a Gamma distribution with shape a and unit rate. Exposed because it is the building block of the chi-square tail used by drftchisq() and benfordtst(): the p-value of a chi-square statistic \(q\) on \(k\) degrees of freedom is \(1 - P(k/2, q/2)\).

Usage

cgamcdf(shape, x)

Arguments

shape

Shape parameter \(a\), a single positive number.

x

Numeric vector of quantiles.

Value

A numeric vector the length of x, each entry a probability in \([0, 1]\).

Details

$$P(a, x) = \frac{1}{\Gamma(a)} \int_0^x t^{a-1} e^{-t} \, dt,$$ evaluated by the shared core (a series for small \(x\), a continued fraction otherwise, the standard pairing), and agreeing with stats::pgamma(x, shape) to rounding. For a gamma distribution with rate \(r\), pass x * r.

shape must be a single positive number ("shape must be a single positive number"). A negative x gives 0, a missing x gives NA, and Inf gives 1, as in stats::pgamma().

See also

stats::pgamma(), the base R equivalent.

Examples

cgamcdf(3.5, c(0.5, 1, 4, 12))
#> [1] 0.005171463 0.040159631 0.667406097 0.998860649

# Identical to the unit-rate gamma CDF.
all.equal(cgamcdf(3.5, c(0.5, 1, 4, 12)),
          stats::pgamma(c(0.5, 1, 4, 12), shape = 3.5))
#> [1] TRUE

# Shape 1 is the exponential distribution.
all.equal(cgamcdf(1, c(0.5, 2)), stats::pexp(c(0.5, 2)))
#> [1] TRUE

# A chi-square tail on k degrees of freedom is 1 - P(k/2, q/2).
1 - cgamcdf(2 / 2, 5.99 / 2)      # about 0.05 on 2 df
#> [1] 0.05003663

# The shape must be positive.
try(cgamcdf(0, 1))
#> Error : `shape` must be a single positive number
